answer: The umber multiplier is published, charged in prism, and ridge lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2154 identities would post 4874 proofs and burn roughly 47 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
